paper.title: Research Ethics Committees as an intervention point to promote a priori sample size calculations

findings.evidence: rec_outcomes() sums the coded outcomes with na.rm = TRUE, so institutions whose form was not obtained (NA codes) drop out of the denominator. Table 1 prints only numerators (US 9, UK 10 for sample size) and never prints the number of forms coded per country, so the reader cannot see that the US share is 9/19 and the UK share 10/14. The number of forms actually coded per country is not reported anywhere in the capsule.

The analysis keeps rows with a non-missing expenditure_rank. Three rows are national bodies rather than universities (National Institutes of Health phase 2, National Institutes of Health behavioural, NHS HRA) and are dropped by that filter; the capsule text does not state this exclusion rule, and the sampling frame ('10 RECs from research-intensive universities in each country') is not in the capsule. Whether the national bodies were part of the intended sample cannot be checked from the materials.

findings.evidence: Abstract: 'template ethics submission forms from 10 RECs from research-intensive universities in each of the United States and the United Kingdom (for 20 forms in total)'. The authors' stored Table 1 (produced by code/analysis.Rmd) reports 'Institutions sampled': US 19, UK 14, i.e. 19 + 14 = 33 institutions, not 10 + 10 = 20. Our Python port of the same code on data/rec_data_raw.csv gives the same 19 and 14 (bp_out/port_results.json). The data file has 36 rows: 21 US and 15 UK, of which 2 US (National Institutes of Health, phase 2 and behavioural) and 1 UK (NHS HRA) have no expenditure_rank and are dropped by the filter in analysis.Rmd:31-32.
